feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform leadership. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive across sections, and could sharpen impact with more outcome-focused metrics and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression strongly support “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”  
- Good credibility: named tools, platforms, team scope, website scale, and concrete initiatives like Drupal migration, analytics stack expansion, and AI search add substance.  
- Writing quality is strong overall: polished tone, no obvious misspellings, and mostly clean grammar with effective action verbs.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to make the CV leaner and easier to scan.  
- Add stronger results language: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes; include measurable impact where possible (engagement, efficiency, adoption, cost/time savings).  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: mixed punctuation/list formatting in experience entries, inconsistent serial comma usage (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs other lists), and “A2/Learning” would read more cleanly as “A2 (learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It would be more impactful with one concrete scale indicator and slightly tighter phrasing to reduce overlap with competencies and experience bullets.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a proof point from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page website,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten the list of responsibilities to 3–4 themes; “platforms, governance models and content operations” plus the second sentence currently feels dense.
- Consider a sharper rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector web ecosystems. Leads enterprise website transformation, digital governance, analytics infrastructure, editorial operations, and AI-enabled content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”
- Keep “public-sector” and “mission-driven organizations,” which are strong positioning terms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Analytics infrastructure,” “editorial systems,” and “AI-enabled user experiences” repeat language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Multimedia production” is better evidenced in experience; consider omitting it here unless it is central to target roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened, made more distinctive, and aligned to the most senior/recent strengths.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording: “Enterprise web modernization,” “Digital governance and editorial operations,” “Analytics, dashboards, and reporting systems.”
- Prioritize highest-value, recent capabilities first; move “Multimedia production and livestream operations” later since it is less central than platform, governance, analytics, and AI.
- Standardize style by using parallel noun phrases and avoiding mixed constructions like “communications operations” vs. “content experiences.”
- Possible rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting systems • AI-enabled search and structured content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with the header summary and all four Topline Skills blocks; consider shortening this section or using it to emphasize only differentiators not listed elsewhere.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is close to “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” in Topline Skills.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the block repeats themes already covered in Work Experience and Core Competencies. It will land better with tighter phrasing, parallel structure, and clearer emphasis on outcomes or scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item consistently: action + platform/channel + purpose/outcome.
- Tighten wording: “hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” is strong; consider “to improve policy-content discovery” for brevity.
- Use parallel verbs and cleaner phrasing, e.g. “Launched a Drupal 10 campaign microsite…” / “Produced a multi-part anniversary campaign…”
- Standardize style: write “10 x 20-foot” (not 10×20-foot) and add commas in all complex lists.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video work substantially overlap with the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- If space is tight, keep only the most distinctive projects here and let Work Experience carry the broader responsibilities.

items.title: Coleman Davis
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear relevance, but it reads as a broad service list rather than a high-impact recent engagement. Tighten around 3–4 outcomes-focused themes and avoid repeating skills already covered in NACo roles and the projects section.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + value: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with stronger ones: “built,” “led,” “streamlined,” “launched,” “improved.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4 bullets max, e.g. platform/campaign build, governance/workflows, technical implementation, AI search initiative.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/templates launched, workflow time reduced, publishing speed improved, search success/engagement gains, stakeholders supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” overlaps with prior NACo bullets; make this specific to the freelance engagement.
- Drupal microsites and AI search also appear in Recent Projects, so keep this item higher-level and reserve build details for the projects section.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact role with good scale metrics, but it reads a bit like a responsibility list. Tighten around 3–4 signature outcomes and make leadership/business impact more explicit.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the website bullets into one sharper achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add outcome language where possible: for analytics/governance, specify what improved (reporting speed, decision-making cadence, publishing consistency, cross-team adoption, cost savings, reduced vendor reliance).
- Rephrase channel/video bullets to emphasize strategic impact: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, expanding internal capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating newsletter/video growth details already covered in the Associate Communications Director role.
- “Governance, publishing standards, and planning systems” overlaps with the current consulting role; keep this entry focused on enterprise-scale transformation.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional ownership, channel growth, and cross-team coordination rather than broad digital leadership.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to focus on operational ownership: “Managed day-to-day execution of NACo’s digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy content delivery.”
- Tighten bullets and start with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and specific: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper point: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows by coordinating communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” is too close to the Director role’s “Led NACo’s digital communications team.”
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier role and footer project; avoid repeating “weekly video updates” elsewhere.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more clearly tied to recent enterprise/public-sector leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with tighter, differentiated skill labels:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “content operations” or “web modernization” to better reflect recent Director/Consultant scope.
- Keep wording noun-based and parallel; avoid mixing leadership traits with execution tasks.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect this section to scale in experience bullets rather than adding metrics here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially repeat the header/Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one version consistently.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution strengths rather than repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, with the most relevant/recent items first.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences • WordPress, SharePoint and Power Pages”
- Drop “jQuery” here unless it is central to current work; it feels dated versus the more strategic tone elsewhere.
- If space allows, use “enterprise web platforms” or “digital platform implementation” as the lead concept to better match seniority.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool lists for the technical section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid overemphasizing it in identical wording.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization” and repeats tools already proven in the recent Director role. Make this section more executive-level by emphasizing outcomes and decision support, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI frameworks, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten wording: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding and decision support.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and KPI design • Executive dashboarding and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • SEO, content performance and conversion analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is highly duplicative of “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; consider making one tools-focused and this one outcomes-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already explicitly covered in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus several NACo bullets. Make it more senior and operational, emphasizing broadcast/studio capability rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Broadcast, Studio & Event Production**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level terms: **Broadcast video production • Livestream and webcast delivery • PTZ and multi-camera studio systems • Hybrid/virtual event production • Studio operations and run-of-show execution**
- If space allows, add one stronger qualifier tied to recent work: **In-house studio buildout and broadcast-quality event delivery**
- Avoid “video production and editing” unless editing is a target-role requirement; it undersells leadership scope.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies; consider keeping multimedia only once.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with NACo studio/event bullets, so keep this skills item concise rather than descriptive.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section above. This item should either be tightened to avoid repetition or reframed to emphasize platform depth and recency.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, modular content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, order by relevance/strength: Drupal first, then WordPress/SharePoint, with GitHub Pages last as lighter-use.
- Consider dropping “GitHub Pages” unless it supports a notable project; it reads less strategic than the rest.
- If you want more impact, rename the heading to “CMS & Web Platforms” for cleaner phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already includes Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- “Drupal” is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid repeating the same platform list in multiple places without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, AI search, and workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as a sharper technical stack line: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Integrations & tagging: APIs, Google Tag Manager • Edge/serverless: Cloudflare Workers • Dev workflow: GitHub Actions”
- Use consistent category labels to improve scanability and reduce the “laundry list” feel.
- If accurate, replace older/general items with more current specifics tied to recent work, e.g. “Drupal front-end theming,” “search implementation,” or “CI/CD automation.”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other tools are also versioned; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- GTM may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function to show stronger systems thinking: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Consider renaming to “Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools” so Slack/Teams feel intentional, not padded.
- If space allows, add a short qualifier instead of only listing tools: “Used to build intake, approval, publishing and cross-team coordination workflows.”
- Prioritize the most relevant/recent tools first; if Jira/Basecamp/Trello were lightly used, trim 1–2 to keep the section sharper.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Airtable and workflow automation already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams may be too generic unless tied to workflow coordination.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal scale or level of use. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent roles, keep this as a concise platform list rather than repeating channel-management claims.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for readability and ATS match: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add level/context in brief parenthetical form: “Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys (automation/journey building) • Higher Logic (member email/community) • Mailchimp (campaigns/newsletters)”
- Keep ordering by strongest/recentest platform first; put the system most used in 2022–present first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “audience engagement,” or “campaign management” language here; those points are already covered in NACo experience.
- Don’t repeat analytics or workflow tooling here; those are already captured under Analytics and Automation sections.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and misses a chance to show depth or specialization. In a technical section, tighten it to platforms/methods and avoid generic nouns.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI/reporting design
- Replace “SEO” with a concrete tool or capability (e.g., Google Search Console, technical SEO, performance analysis).
- Replace “Dashboarding” with a sharper skill phrase like “KPI/reporting design” or “executive dashboards.”
- If space allows elsewhere, tie these tools to impact in recent roles rather than listing them twice.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Nearly duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” (same tools plus SEO/performance analysis).
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role; avoid repeating all of them in multiple sections unless this section is kept very concise.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs or scale if you can add them.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve execution across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add specific scope/results where possible: website refresh size, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, audience reach, or process improvements.
- Tighten the close: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and supervised a digital media associate’s day-to-day work.”
- If accurate, emphasize systems built that enabled later growth: templates, publishing workflows, content calendars, or cross-channel coordination.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version focused on launching/establishing the format, not expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is repeated elsewhere; specify foundational processes or tools introduced here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the most distinctive achievement: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation, research support, and first-of-its-kind multimedia work.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities, while expanding NACo’s early digital content capabilities.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and tighten phrasing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague wording like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a sharper phrase such as “produced digital and multimedia content for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of research/projects coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating generic multimedia/digital production language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here; later positions better establish management and enterprise ownership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item is currently a mixed list of software and capabilities. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, and let the experience section carry the stronger production/studio impact.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Multimedia & Creative Software
- Rewrite as: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator
- If you want to keep one workflow item, use: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Podcast editing
- Only include tools you actively used in recent roles; if applicable, add stronger current tools instead of generic workflow phrases
